title: Animation Import
content: **Objective** Import Animation cache data created in the third-party 3D solutions. **※ Note:** Refer to the links below for FBX/ Alembic file import:. * [3D File (FBX) Import/Export ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000526908-3D%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-FBX-%EB%B6%88%EB%9F%AC%EC%98%A4%EA%B8%B0-%EB%82%B4%EB%B3%B4%EB%82%B4%EA%B8%B0) * [3D File (Alembic) Import/Export](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000499067-3D%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-Alembic-%EB%B6%88%EB%9F%AC%EC%98%A4%EA%B8%B0-%EB%82%B4%EB%B3%B4%EB%82%B4%EA%B8%B0) ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Animation ▶ * **Maya Cache(.mc) ** * **Maya Cache(.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache(Standard) ** * **MDD Cache(Maya/3ds Max)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Animation ▶ * **Maya Cache(.mc) ** * **Maya Cache(.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache(Standard) ** * **MDD Cache(Maya/3ds Max)** → The File Explorer or Find window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click**OK**. → An option window appears with settings that apply to the file format selected. 3. Set the following individual settings. **Object** | **Select All Avatars** | Apply the cache data to all objects in the 3D environment. Cache data can be applied to individual objects from the submenu. ---|---|--- **FPS** | Set the frame rate of the cache data. **※ Note:** This menu only appears when importing Point Cache (PC2) files. **Scale** | Set the scale of the cache data. **Axis Conversion** | Set the axis direction for the cache data. The Y-axis runs vertically by default. **Garment Position** | **Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position** | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). **Transition Animation** | A transition animation is an animation that changes from a T-pose to a motion’s first pose in stages, and is created when the avatar’s current pose and motion differs from that of the first frame pose. 4. Click **OK**. → The cache data is imported according to the selected settings.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing animation cache data from various third-party 3D solutions, including step-by-step instructions and file format specifications.

title: Change Pose by Collada's Joint Information
content: **Objective** **※ Note:** Only available for file formats with avatar joint information. In this case, COLLADA is being used. As avatar's joints move as the pose changes, it is able to change avatar pose while keeping the stimulation stably even if there is a large difference between the starting and the end poses. However if the avatar is formatted via DAZ Studio, some composition form information may be lost during the process. Therefore there is a need to load the posed avatar's OBJ file and adjust garments after changing the pose. (The avatar's OBJ file only saves the composition form information, there is no danger of losses in the loading process.) ** Operation** 1. Export a T-pose avatar which can be easily draped and an avatar with the final pose in COLLADA files. To find out export methods from DAZ Studio and Poser in details, check [3D File (COLLADA) Import](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000531948) for the reference. 2. After exporting the COLLADA files, export the avatar poses in OBJ files. 3. Load a posed COLLADA file from the previously saved avatars in CLO 3D/MD. 4. Click File ▶ Save ▶ **Pose** to save current avatar as POS file. After dressing T-pose avatar, this file is going to be used when changing current pose. 5. Click File ▶ Open ▶ **Avatar** to open the previously saved T-pose COLLADA file. Dress the avatar with desired garments. 6. Now Click File ▶ Open ▶ **Pose** to open the previously saved POS file. The avatar slowly changes poses. It may take a while depending on the complexity of the garments. 7. After the pose changes, load an OBJ file without any loss and adjust garments. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** to open the previously saved final pose OBJ file. Highly positive to observe garments being under the avatar's surface. 8. While simulation is being activated, drag out the parts that are gone under the avatar's surface by using left mouse button. To find more details in **Select/Move** tool, check [Move Garment](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000304968) for the reference.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adjusting and dressing avatars in CLO 3D/MD using COLLADA and OBJ file formats to ensure accurate pose transitions and garment fitting.

title: Physical Property Detail Setting
content: Adjust each item of the detailed settings to express Physical Properties not included in Presets. Each property mutually affects one another and a Garment's physical property is expressed by combination of all detailed property values. **※ Note:** * The property details are adjustable with the scroll bar or by entering in actual measurement values. ** ** * **Scroll Bar [0~99]** : This is better input method when the constant value is far too enormous. To reduce this inconvenience, the most commonly used Physical Property is split into 99 stages. * **Constant Value [0~1000000000]** This is better input method when setting far more accurate Physical Properties than the scroll bar method above.
content_description: Customize and fine-tune the physical properties of your garment by adjusting detailed settings, ensuring a precise expression of unique characteristics through interactive sliders and accurate measurement inputs.

title: Edit Button Style
content: **List of Contents** Edit Button Style Edit Properties Open/Save Button Style **Edit Button Style ** \- Edit properties for the button style. \- Select a button style from the Object Browser ▶ **Button Tab** and view the selected button’s properties in the Property Editor. **Edit Properties ** * **Button Name** \- Rename the selected button style. * **Shape** \- Rename the selected button style. \- Click the drop-down arrow next to the Shape menu to view all default button shapes. \- Select the desired button shape. \- The shape is applied to the button. * **Width** \- Set the width of the button style. \- The width’s unit follows the unit configured by the user in the settings. \- To use Ligne (L) as the width unit, please navigate to Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Others ▶ Unit and toggle on the **Use Ligne (L) for Button Width** option. * **Thickness** \- Set the thickness of the button style. * **Weight** \- Set the weight of the button style in grams. **Open/Save Button Style ** * **Open** \- Click the Open button on the top of the Property Editor to load previously saved button style. * **Save** \- Click the Save button on the top of the Property Editor to save the configured button style. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing, saving, and customizing button styles, including options for shape, width, thickness, and weight.

title: Register Custom Buttonholes
content: **List of Contents** Register Buttonhole Add Buttonhole **Register Buttonhole **\- Use custom images as buttonholes. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials ▶ Button ▶**Register Buttonhole. ** \- Or, select a desired buttonhole style from the Object Browser ▶ **Buttonhole Tab**. Then, navigate to the Property Editor to find the **Register Buttonhole** button next to the Shape toggle down menu. ** Add Buttonhole ** \- Select the **Register Buttonhole** button by following the path above. \- The **Register Buttonhole** window appears. \- Name the buttonhole. \- Select the **+** button next to the Image menu to upload a buttonhole image. \- Select OK to complete the registration. \- The registered buttonhole shows in the following path: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Buttonhole (Select a Style) ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Shape.** \- The registered buttonhole is automatically saved to CLO-ENTERPRISE ▶ Assets_ver. x. x. xx ▶ Preferences ▶ Button_Preset. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for users to register and add custom buttonholes in the CLO-Enterprise software.

title: Scale OBJ Trims
content: **List of Contents** Transform OBJ Trims Scale OBJ Dimension **Transform OBJ Trims **\- Transform OBJ files loaded as trim as needed. \- Select the imported OBJ file loaded as trim and select the**Scale button** hovering over the trim. \- Select the OBJ file loaded as trim and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Scale OBJ Dimension** * **Via the Scale Gizmo ** \- Load an OBJ file as a trim. \- Click on the OBJ and select the **Scale button** on the right top corner. \- The **Scale Gizmo** is formed with three axes and one square. \- Select the Scale button again to complete the transformation. * **Axis** \- Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. \- Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. \- Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. * **Square** \- Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ, maintaining its x,y,z dimensional ratio. * **Via the Property Editor ** \- Select the OBJ trim to be scaled. \- The selected OBJ’s properties appear in the Property Editor. \- Find and adjust properties under the Scale (Local) menu as needed. * **Scale (Local)** \- X： Type in the value to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. \- Y： Type in the value to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. \- Z： Type in the value to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. \- **Lock Aspect Ratio** : Transform the OBJ file while maintaining its dimensional ratio. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on transforming and scaling OBJ trim files using both the Scale Gizmo and Property Editor for precise 3D modifications.

The 2D window is adjusted automatically to show all Patterns maintaining the current view. **Without Patterns** * **3D Window** \- Right click on the 3D window to open the pop-up menu. \- When the pop-up menu appears, select **Zoom Extents All**. title: Order of Use of the Modular Configurator Window
content: Follow the order of use of the Modualr Configurator window in order to construct and use an user data. To create a configuration file for the Modular Configurator, please follow the steps below: Open the Modular Configurator window ▶ Add an User folder by pressing (**+**) icon ▶ Press the **Edit** icon to switch to the Editor Mode ▶ If needed, add groups by pressing **Add Group** icon ▶ Designate the Modular file (.zmdr) to either be displayed or hidden for each group ▶ Designate the Modular file (.zblc) to either be displayed or hidden for each group ▶ Click **Save** button to save the structure file in the same folder as the Block ▶ Press **Exit** button when editing is done
content_description: Learn how to effectively use the Modular Configurator to create and manage user data configurations step-by-step.

title: General Process of Using Modular Mode
content: Follow the procedure of the Modular Mode to build and design with your own Pattern database. To build the Pattern database, take following procedures: Open Modular Template ▶ Add Patterns or Garments ▶ Drag the Patterns into Block Boxes ▶ Sew the Patterns and the Block Boxes ▶ Save it as a Block file (If there is no Modular file in a folder where the Blocks are being saved, save a Modular file too)
content_description: "Learn how to create and customize your own Pattern database using the Modular Mode through a step-by-step guide."

title: Adjust Collision Thickness
content: **Objective** Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. **※ Note:** For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that [Skin Offset](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002227387) is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. **Location** Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Simulation Thickness property for garment patterns to optimize collision limits and achieve smooth fabric simulation.

title: Delete All Overlapping Points
content: **Objective** Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When importing *.dxf files created in other CAD programs or cutting Patterns in CLO, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by CLO. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Delete All Overlapping Points** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Delete All Overlapping Points** → All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to delete overlapping points in patterns and internal shapes within CLO to ensure proper functionality and editing of imported CAD files.

title: Fabric Information Preview
content: **Fabric Information Preview ** **-** Preview fabric information in the Library Window. \- Hover the mouse over the fabric (.zfab) file in the Library Window for about 0.5 second. \- The preview of fabric information will appear on the right. \- Only fabric (.zfab) files saved in v.3.1.0 or higher versions can see the preview. \- To preview fabrics saved in previous versions, save the same fabric (.zfab) files in v.3.1.0 or higher versions. Then, open updated fabric (.zfab) files.
content_description: "Quickly access and preview detailed information about your fabric files in the Library Window by hovering over them, ensuring compatibility with version 3.1.0 or higher."

title: Replace as Pattern Outline
content: **Replace as Pattern Outline ** **-** Swap Internal Line and Pattern Outline to replace Internal Line as Pattern Outline. \- Select **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D Window. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select Internal Line and Pattern Outline to be swapped. \- Selected Internal Line and Pattern Outline will be highlighted in yellow. \- Right click on the selected lines to access a pop-up menu. \- Select **Replace as Pattern Outline.** \- The selected Pattern Outline will be replaced with the selected Internal Line as original Pattern Outline will appear as Baseline.
content_description: Learn how to easily swap an Internal Line with a Pattern Outline in your design using the **Replace as Pattern Outline** feature.

title: Pleats Fold
content: **List of Contents** Pleats Fold Using Pleats Fold Pleats Fold Options **Pleats Fold** \- Auto assign fold angles based on the direction of the pleats. \- Select the **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D toolbar. **Using Pleats Fold** \- Select the **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. \- Click on the pattern to designate the start point of the pleats direction. Then, drag the mouse towards the direction the pleats will be folded. \- Double click to complete the guide line. \- Make sure to encompass all internal lines that fold angles should be assigned to. \- The Pleats Fold Window will appear. **Pleats Fold Options** * **Pleats Type ** \- Select the desired pleats type among following options: knife pleats, box pleats, and accordion pleats. * **Options**** ** * **REVERSE DIRECTION -**Change the fold direction of the pleats * **FOLD ANGLE** \- Set fold angle range that will be applied to the pleats pattern. \- Choose among Preset or enter the desired value. * **NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS** \- Decide whether two or three internal lines will be included per pleats. \- If internal lines that are supposed to have 180° fold angles are not established within the pleats pattern, select two for NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS. \- After the adjusting the options, hit OK. \- The outside folds will be highlighted in red whereas the inside folds will be highlighted in green. \- The pleats pattern will be folded based on the settings when the Simulation is activated. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to using the Pleats Fold tool, including instructions on selecting pleat types, setting fold angles, and customizing internal line options for accurate pleat design.
